sections.html:
Gary sits on the southern shore of Lake Michigan in Lake County, about 25 miles southeast of Chicago. It covers about 50.7 square miles and contains the western portion of Indiana Dunes National Park, including Miller Woods. Lake County is Indiana's second-most populous county, and its seat is Crown Point.

U.S. Steel founded Gary in 1906 as a company town for its Gary Works plant, and the city grew with the mill. Jobs at Gary Works fell from over 30,000 in the early 1970s to 6,000 in 1990 and 2,246 in 2023. Lake County's steel employment dropped from over 60,000 in the 1960s to about 18,000 by 2015.

YearGary population

The population has fallen about 61 percent since 1960. Heavy industry still anchors the economy, and a $300 million Hard Rock casino opened in May 2021.

The 2020 census counted 37,274 housing units in Gary, and 23.2 percent of them were vacant. The rental vacancy rate was 9.9 percent and the homeowner vacancy rate was 2.8 percent.

The city runs a demolition program aimed at unsafe structures. In 2024 it demolished 35 structures in Aetna, with over 20 more planned for 2025, and construction firms and the Lake County Highway Department volunteered their services. Before any demolition, the Department of Redevelopment reviews each property under Indiana's Unsafe Building Law, which includes identifying the property, notifying owners and assessing condition.

A citywide blight campaign targets about 60 unsafe structures in Downtown, Emerson, Glen Park, Midtown and Westside. The city has also piloted a multi-department approach with smoke alarms, patrols and rodent abatement.

If you own a house the city has flagged, respond to the notice. A flagged house can still be sold, but the buyer will want to know about the notice and any deadline on it.

Gary's neighborhoods include Downtown Gary, Downtown West, Emerson, Ambridge Mann, Brunswick, Tolleston, Black Oak, Glen Park, Midtown, Aetna and Miller Beach. Broadway divides downtown into two areas, and Miller Beach is the easternmost neighborhood, bordering the Indiana Dunes.

Three public districts serve the city. The Gary Community School Corporation covers most of it, Lake Ridge Schools Corporation serves Black Oak and unincorporated Calumet Township, and River Forest Community School Corporation serves a small southeastern portion. Several charter schools also operate here.

Gary/Chicago International Airport is an alternative to Chicago's two larger airports. The South Shore Line commuter rail runs between Chicago and South Bend, and the Gary Public Transportation Corporation operates local service. Interstates I-90, I-80, I-94 and I-65 all reach the city, along with U.S. routes 6, 12 and 20 and State Road 912 (Cline Avenue). The Cline Avenue bridge was closed for eleven years and reopened in 2020.

For a buyer who works in Chicago, the rail line and the interstates are worth pointing out when you describe the house.

July and August highs average about 84 degrees Fahrenheit, and January and February highs about 29. Precipitation averages about 40 inches a year, and snowfall about 25 inches, with lake-effect snow common.

Vacant houses feel that weather first, since nobody is there to clear snow, watch for leaks or keep heat on. If your Gary house has been empty through a winter, document its condition with dated photos before you talk with any buyer.

Gary requires owners of residential rental units to register them each year under Ordinance C.P.O. 2012-79. The Building Department lists the fee as $5 per single-family home.

  • For multi-unit properties the fee is $5 per unit, up to four units.
  • Enrollment runs from January 1 through March 30 each year.
  • Late registration adds $25 per property.
  • Noncompliance may bring fines starting at $250.

Ask the Building Department what inspections apply to your property. City Hall is at 401 Broadway, with public hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Central Time, Monday through Friday.

The Lake County Treasurer collects Gary's property tax at 2293 N. Main Street, Crown Point, IN 46307. The phone is 219-755-3760, and the county's online Tax Search page is the way to pay. Halves come due in May and November. Pay within 30 days after a due date and you owe a 5 percent penalty, as long as no back taxes exist. Past that, the penalty becomes 10 percent.

sections.h2: Tax sale rules and back taxes
sections.html:
Falling behind can end in a tax sale. Each year the county builds a delinquent list, on or before July 1 or 51 days after the due date. Every owner on it gets a certified letter, and two local newspapers print names and addresses. Bidding takes place wholly online within 171 days of certification, and the lowest allowed bid equals everything owed on the parcel. Parcels that find no bidder pass to the Board of Commissioners. The governing laws are Indiana Code 6-1.1-24 and 6-1.1-25.

If you are behind, ask the treasurer for a payoff statement and think about selling before the certification date.

A sale for money also brings a Sales Disclosure Form, which both parties sign and the county auditor files once the assessor has reviewed it. Expect a $20 fee, except in cases like foreclosure, divorce or probate.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a house in Gary
sections.html:
Your options are an agent, a sale by owner, or a cash offer, and the condition of the house and the block carry the most weight.

  • Listing is for a house that shows well, when you can wait out a buyer's loan.
  • Selling yourself saves the fee but leaves you with the paperwork.
  • A cash offer fits a house that is vacant, damaged, inherited, behind on taxes or under a city notice.

We buy Gary houses as they are, and an offer carries no obligation.

Here is how it goes. You give us the address and a description of the house, including whether it is empty and whether the city has sent any notice. We tour the property and make an offer in writing. If you accept, a title company searches the title, finds any tax balance or lien, and prepares the deed. Closing happens on the date you choose, and payoffs come out of your proceeds.

Bring what you have: the latest tax statement, any city notice with its deadline, dated photos of a vacant house, and for an inherited house the estate papers and names of all heirs. No appraisal is involved, so the sale does not depend on a bank. Expect the offer to come in under a fully renovated retail sale, and weigh it against what a listing would net after repairs, commission and the months you would carry the house.

faqs.q: What county is Gary, Indiana in?
faqs.a: Gary is in Lake County, on the southern shore of Lake Michigan. The county seat is Crown Point.

faqs.q: How many homes in Gary are vacant?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 37,274 housing units in Gary, and 23.2 percent were vacant.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Gary house that has a city unsafe-building notice?
faqs.a: Yes, a flagged house can still be sold. The notice and its deadlines should be disclosed to the buyer, and you can ask the city where the case stands.

faqs.q: When are Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Each May and November. Up to 30 days late adds 5 percent, and later than that adds 10 percent.

faqs.q: Do Gary landlords have to register rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. Registration runs January 1 through March 30 each year, at $5 per single-family home, with a $25 late fee and fines starting at $250 for noncompliance.
